defects.description: The lower-bound search shrinks the upper bound to `mid - 1` instead of `mid`, breaking the invariant, so `_find_start` can return a resume index that is too small and the page re-emits an item the caller was already handed.
paraphrases: When the probe lands past the boundary the loop discards the midpoint by moving the high end below it, which can skip the true first-greater position and cause an already-seen row to reappear at the top of the next page.

The half-open search invariant requires keeping the midpoint as the new ceiling; dropping it by one collapses the window prematurely and yields a start offset that duplicates the previous page's last element.
Excluding `mid` from the still-viable range corrupts the resume-point computation, so paginating past a cursor can hand back a boundary record twice instead of continuing strictly after it.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '            hi = mid'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The page window slice ends at `start + page_size + 1`, so every page returns one more item than the requested `page_size`, violating the page-size contract.
paraphrases: Each fetched window grabs an extra trailing element beyond the caller's limit, inflating the returned batch by one row per page.
The upper index of the page slice overshoots by a single position, meaning a request for N results consistently yields N+1.
Because the window's end offset is one too large, the returned item count exceeds the configured page size on every call.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '    window = view[start : start + page_size]'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: `Page.is_last` returns `has_more` directly rather than its negation, so the method reports True precisely when more pages remain and False on the final page.
paraphrases: The final-page predicate is flipped: it claims there is a last page whenever further pages exist and denies it once the collection is actually exhausted.
Dropping the negation makes `is_last` a synonym for `has_more`, giving callers the opposite of the intended end-of-stream signal.
The helper answers whether iteration should continue instead of whether it has finished, inverting the terminal-page check.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        return not self.has_more'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The constant-time comparison AND-accumulates the per-character differences into a zero-initialized accumulator, so the result stays 0 for every input and the checksum is treated as matching even when it does not, disabling tamper detection.
paraphrases: Because differences are folded together with `&=` starting from zero, the running total can never leave zero, so `_constant_time_equals` always reports equality and forged tokens sail through validation.
The digest comparison collapses to a constant success verdict: the bitwise-and reduction against an initial 0 masks any real byte divergence, letting an altered checksum pass as authentic.
Accumulating XOR diffs via and-assignment instead of or-assignment nullifies them all, meaning a tampered cursor whose body was edited is accepted rather than rejected.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        mismatch |= ord(x) ^ ord(y)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.
